claim.title: Rapid Task-Type Identification (Posterior Concentration)
claim.statement: In a mixture of task types, the inference-time error (MSE) of a sufficiently pretrained Transformer rapidly approaches the 'Bayes (oracle)' curve (which assumes knowledge of the true task family) as the number of in-context examples k increases, demonstrating that the task-type identification error vanishes exponentially fast.
claim.test_plan: Pretrain a Transformer on a mixture of two distinct regression tasks (e.g., linear and non-linear) with large N and p to minimize the Bayes Gap. At inference time, evaluate the MSE for k = 1 to 20 in-context examples. Compare the Transformer's MSE curve to two baselines: 'Bayes (mixture)' (posterior mean over all tasks) and 'Bayes (oracle)' (posterior mean for the true task only). Measure the gap between Transformer MSE and Oracle MSE.
claim.success_criterion: The gap between the Transformer's MSE and the Bayes (oracle) MSE decreases monotonically with k and is less than 10% of the initial gap (at k=1) by k=5.
